privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: Anatomy listens to music so you can understand it. This policy explains, plainly, what happens to what it hears — and why your audio stays on your device.

body: Anatomy is a music analysis app made by NoSky Studios Ltd. It listens to music — live through the microphone, in your headphones, or from a file you import — names it, and helps you understand and play with it.

We do not have accounts. We do not ask you to sign in. We do not run analytics, advertising, or tracking of any kind. Your recordings, imported songs, and everything Anatomy works out about them are stored on your device and are never sent to us.
All musical analysis happens on your device. The rest of this policy explains the few places data does move — always for a feature you used, and never to a server we control.
Anatomy is published by NoSky Studios Ltd (RC 7631695), a company registered in Nigeria ("NoSky Studios", "we", "us", or "our").
This Privacy Policy applies to the Anatomy iOS app, its widgets, and its Live Activities. For any privacy question, contact us at [privacy@noskystudios.ng](mailto:privacy@noskystudios.ng).
We want to be specific, because "we value your privacy" means little on its own. In Anatomy there is:
list: No account and no sign-in. You do not create a profile, and we never ask for your name, email, or phone number to use the app.

No analytics or usage tracking. Anatomy contains no analytics, crash-reporting, advertising, or attribution software, and no third-party code libraries of any kind. We do not measure how you use the app.
No advertising identifiers. Anatomy does not request the App Tracking Transparency permission and does not access the device advertising identifier (IDFA).
No uploading of your audio. Your recordings and imported songs are never uploaded — not to us, and not to anyone else.
No selling or sharing of data. We do not sell, rent, or share your personal information, because we do not receive it in the first place.

body: Everything Anatomy keeps is stored locally on your device, in storage private to the app and its widgets. This includes:
list: Your song library: each song's title, artist, genre, artwork, identification details (such as its Shazam ID, ISRC code, and Apple Music link), when it was added, and how it was captured (live, from headphones, or imported).
Audio: your live recordings, the songs you import, and — for songs heard through headphones — Apple's 30-second preview of the song rather than a recording.
Analysis results: key, tempo, loudness, song structure, chords, lyrics, the separated parts of a song (vocals, drums, bass, and so on), and any remixed versions you create.
Preferences: your settings, where you left off in the player, and, for each Bluetooth or USB audio device you connect, its name and whether you told Anatomy it is headphones or a speaker.
Lyrics you paste or import from a text file. Anatomy reads your clipboard only when you tap to paste.
after: This information stays on your device unless you deliberately share it, for example with the share sheet. Anatomy does not use iCloud sync and has no cloud copy of your library. Your recordings and library are included in your normal device backups (such as an encrypted iPhone or iCloud device backup) that you control through Apple, not through us; separated parts and remixes are excluded from those backups and can be recreated.

body: When you listen live, Anatomy uses the microphone to hear the music around you, and saves what it hears (up to six minutes) as a recording on your device. When you import a song, it reads the audio file you chose. In both cases, every part of the analysis — key, tempo, loudness, structure, chords, splitting a song into its parts, and remixing — is computed on your device using models built into the app and into iOS.

If you ask Anatomy to write out a song's lyrics, it uses Apple's on-device speech recognition. The first time, iOS may need to download Apple's speech language model for that language; this happens only after you agree, and it is a download from Apple, not an upload of your audio.
Recordings and imported audio never leave your device in playable form.
Anatomy's analysis works offline. It makes a small number of network requests, only to power specific features, and never to send us your data. Here is the complete list:
list: Song identification (Apple Shazam). To name a song you listen to or import, Anatomy uses Apple's ShazamKit. ShazamKit sends Apple a compact acoustic signature — a fingerprint of the sound, not a recording that can be played back — and Apple returns the song's details. If you choose "Add to Shazam Library", the song is saved to your own Shazam library, which Apple keeps.

Song previews and details (Apple iTunes Search). For songs heard through headphones, Anatomy sends the song's title and artist, or its Apple Music ID, together with your device's region code, to Apple's iTunes Search service to fetch the song's 30-second preview, which is then analysed on your device. The same kind of request is used to look up a song's genre or its length when Anatomy needs them.
Artwork. Cover images for identified songs are downloaded once from Apple's servers and cached on your device.

Opening a song in another service (song.link). If you choose to open a song in Spotify or YouTube Music, Anatomy sends the song's Apple Music link to song.link (Odesli) to find the same song there. Opening a song in Apple Music, Spotify, or YouTube Music opens that service with the song's title and artist as the search.

Importing from a link. If you paste a web link to import a song, Anatomy downloads the file directly from that address. Dropbox and Google Drive share links are converted to their direct-download form. Only the link you pasted is contacted.
Apple services. Purchases go through Apple's App Store, and speech language models for lyrics are downloaded from Apple when you agree.
after: These providers receive only the information described above, as the operators of the services Anatomy contacts on your behalf, and their use of it is governed by their own privacy policies: [Apple's Privacy Policy](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/) (which covers Shazam and iTunes), [Odesli](https://odesli.co/privacy), and the policy of any website you import from. As with any internet request, these providers may receive your device's IP address and standard request information; we do not receive that information and do not combine it with anything about you.
You can avoid these requests by importing songs from your device rather than listening live, and by not using the streaming-service or link-import features.

body: Anatomy can let you feel music through your iPhone's haptics. For songs that Apple supports, Anatomy passes the song's ISRC (a standard recording code) to Apple's Music Haptics feature on your device. Haptics are generated on your device.
Anatomy Pro — a one-time App Store purchase, not a subscription — is needed to use Anatomy. All purchases are handled by Apple through the App Store using your Apple Account.

Payment is processed entirely by Apple. Anatomy never sees or receives your card, bank, or payment details. To manage your purchase, the app receives from Apple only the fact that a valid purchase exists — not your identity or payment information. Purchases, restores, and refunds are governed by Apple's terms and [Apple's Privacy Policy](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/).
Anatomy asks for a permission only when you use the feature that needs it, and explains why at the moment it asks:
list: Microphone — only to listen to music live. The audio is analysed on your device; only the acoustic signature described above is sent to Apple's Shazam to name the song.
Media & Apple Music — only to import songs you have bought or synced to your device. Copy-protected Apple Music streaming songs cannot be imported.
Speech recognition — only to write out a song's lyrics, on your device.
Notifications — only to tell you when a song has finished splitting into its parts, or could not be split. These are local notifications generated on your device.
after: To import the sound from a video, Anatomy uses Apple's system video picker, which shows only the item you choose and does not give Anatomy access to your photo library. Anatomy reads which audio output is in use (for example, Bluetooth headphones) to ask whether it is headphones or a speaker; it does not request Bluetooth access.
Anatomy does not request location, contacts, camera, health, or tracking permissions. You can review or change any permission at any time in the iOS Settings app.

body: Anatomy's notifications are local notifications, scheduled and delivered on your device. Anatomy does not use push notifications and does not register your device with any messaging server. We cannot send you messages, and we do not know whether or when a notification is shown.

Anatomy's widgets and Live Activities show information from your library — such as the song you are working with and its progress — on your Home Screen, Lock Screen, and Dynamic Island. The app and its widgets share this data in a private, on-device storage area reserved for the app. It never leaves your device.

Anatomy is a general-audience music app and is not directed to children. We do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone, including children under the age of 13 (or the equivalent minimum age in your country). Because Anatomy has no accounts and collects no personal information, there is no such information for us to hold or delete.
Your Anatomy data is stored on your device and is protected by the security of iOS, including the device passcode, encryption, and app sandboxing that Apple provides.

Because your data does not sit on our servers, the most important protection is the one you control: keep your device locked with a passcode or biometrics, and keep iOS up to date. No method of storage or transmission is completely secure, but keeping your data on-device removes the large, central target that a cloud database would present.

You decide how long your data is kept, because you hold it. You can delete any song from your library at any time. In Settings → Storage, "Clear Parts" removes separated parts, lyrics, chords, and remixes while keeping your songs, and "Delete All Songs" removes your whole library. Deleting the Anatomy app removes its library, recordings, and settings from that device. Copies remain in any device backups you made, and songs you added to your Shazam library stay there until you remove them in Shazam.
We hold no copy of your data, so there is nothing for you to request from us and nothing for us to delete on your behalf.

Depending on where you live, data-protection laws — such as the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, the EU and UK General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA/CPRA) — give you rights over your personal information, including the rights to access, correct, delete, and port it, and to object to certain processing.

Anatomy is designed so that you already have these rights directly: your information is on your device, where you can view, change, share, and delete it yourself, at any time, without asking us. We do not collect, store, sell, or share your personal information, and we do not "sell" or "share" it for advertising as those terms are defined under the CCPA.

If you believe we hold personal information about you, or you have a question about your rights, contact us at [privacy@noskystudios.ng](mailto:privacy@noskystudios.ng) and we will respond. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with your local data-protection authority.

Anatomy is available worldwide, and your data stays on your device wherever you are. When you use an online feature (song identification, previews, artwork, streaming-service links, or link import), the request is handled by that provider, which may process it on servers in another country. Those requests contain only the limited information described in the "Network connections" section above.

We may update this Privacy Policy as Anatomy evolves or as the law requires. When we do, we will change the "Effective" date at the top of this page and, for significant changes, note them in the app or its release notes. The current version always lives at this address. Continuing to use Anatomy after an update means you accept the revised policy.

For any question about this policy or your privacy, reach us at [privacy@noskystudios.ng](mailto:privacy@noskystudios.ng). For general help with the app, contact [appstore@noskystudios.ng](mailto:appstore@noskystudios.ng).
